description:
The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) in Pasadena, CA, is hiring an Applied Scientist to lead integration research and development for superconducting quantum devices. You will design, model, and test the chip-to-chip, chip-to-package, and signal-delivery interfaces that let superconducting quantum computers scale, and you will characterize integrated assemblies at cryogenic temperatures to learn how integration choices affect qubit performance, yield, and manufacturability.

You will join a multi-disciplinary team of theoretical and experimental physicists, materials scientists, and hardware and software engineers working at the forefront of quantum computing. You will carry integration technologies from concept through hardware demonstration, build the test standards and automation that make results reproducible across devices, and collaborate with fabrication, hardware, and circuit design engineers to remove the dominant sources of yield loss. You will also contribute to multi-year roadmap planning for integration and scaling capabilities and help establish the scientific foundation for this capability area within the Device team.


Key job responsibilities
In this role you will develop the integration technologies that let superconducting quantum computers scale. Your work will span four connected areas:

- Integration research and development: Design, model, and test integration solutions for superconducting quantum devices, including chip-to-chip, chip-to-package, and signal-delivery interfaces. Build electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical models to predict and optimize performance, and characterize integrated assemblies at cryogenic temperatures.
- Scaling technologies: Develop and evaluate approaches to scaling superconducting quantum hardware against yield, reusability, manufacturability, and scalability, and carry the most promising ones from concept through hardware demonstration.
- Test standards and automation: Define test standards that give rigorous, reproducible measurements of how integration affects qubit coherence, loss, and crosstalk. Automate data collection and reporting against these standards so characterization scales across devices and configurations.
- Yield and manufacturability: Work with fabrication, hardware, printed circuit board, and circuit design engineers to identify and remove the largest sources of yield loss and integration uncertainty, and to design processes and components that are reused across device generations and manufactured at scale.


About the team
The Device team at the AWS Center for Quantum Computing designs, builds, and measures the superconducting quantum devices at the heart of our processors, and develops the integration and packaging that turn individual devices into working systems. You will work alongside physicists, materials scientists, and hardware and software engineers across design, fabrication, measurement, and theory, in a lab built for rapid iteration from concept to cryogenic test. Over the coming years the team's focus is making superconducting quantum hardware scale, and this role establishes integration as a scientific capability area within that effort.

We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

As a member of the UC organization, you'll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (IoT), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS. Mentorship & Career Growth: We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance: We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud.

- Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
- Master's degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, material science, physics or equivalent
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- 3+ years of experience in device integration, cryogenic packaging design/testing, microwave engineering, or quantum hardware characterization
- Experience with cryogenic systems or low-temperature measurement
- Experience using Unix/Linux
- Experience in professional software development
- PhD in electrical engineering, computer science, mathematics or physics
- Hands-on experience integrating superconducting quantum devices, such as multi-chip assembly, interposers, through-substrate interconnects, or cryogenic signal delivery
- Knowledge of sources of decoherence, loss, and crosstalk in superconducting qubit systems related to integration, interfaces, and off-chip environments
- Experience designing for yield, reusability, and manufacturability in microelectronic or cryogenic hardware, including developing test standards and process controls
- Track record of driving R&D from concept through hardware demonstration
